newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane rises slightly on crude rebound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane rises slightly on crude rebound.

text.p: Spot prices of U.S. propane, a key liquefied petroleum gas, rose slightly in late trade on Thursday on the back of NYMEX crude oil's technical bounce, players said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, propane rose a quarter cent to between 34.25 cents and 35.50 cents a gallon after falling 0.75 cent on bearish inventory data.
May barrels were done at 34.25 cents and 34.50 cents.
Conway, Kansas, spot material followed suit, rising a quarter cent to on par with Belvieu.
Both materials rose earlier in the day following release of the Energy Information Administration report, which reported a 1.5 million barrel build in stocks for the week.

The butane markets, however, continued their slide due to a lack of demand and good supply. Belvieu was down to 37.50/38.00 in late trade, a half cent under midday activity. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
